Never modify anything else.

FINDINGS TO FIX:
1. HIGH heal_apply.py ~:187 (residual) — live apply validates the playbook's failure-class against the incident but the {unit} command parameter stays caller-controlled, so a valid timer_failed incident can restart an UNRELATED user unit. Fix: derive the unit (and any path parameter) EXCLUSIVELY from the bound incident's evidence entries (the 'systemd://<unit>' and filesystem-path conventions sense_estate writes); refuse (refused row, nothing executed) when the evidence does not name exactly one unit, or when any caller-supplied parameter disagrees with the derived value. Caller parameters may narrow nothing — they are at most a redundant confirmation.
2. HIGH compare_charter.py ~:129 — observations are collapsed by SUBJECT alone, so a later manifest OK sharing a subject can suppress a publish-day failure for the same subject. Fix: collapse/deduplicate by the (sensor, subject) pair everywhere; add a test with two same-subject observations from different sensors where the failure must survive.
3. HIGH manifest_sensor.py ~:41 — an empty guests list emits NO observation, so absent manifest evidence is invisible (or inherits stale state downstream). Fix: the sensor ALWAYS emits at least one observation per cycle: with guests, per-guest rows as today; with a present-but-empty guest list, one summary row (subject 'manifest-coverage', status ok, detail 'zero active guests in source'); with a missing/unreadable source, the existing unknown behavior. Test all three shapes.
4. HIGH escalate_outbox.py ~:53 — crash-replay dedupe trusts ANY outbox row carrying a matching fingerprint+marker, so a forged or foreign row suppresses the real escalation. Fix: a row only counts for dedupe when it structurally matches our own emission schema: department == 'podcast', the escalation kind/type field our writer sets, the exact state-generation marker, and the issue/fingerprint fields in our format; anything else is ignored (and a malformed row in the outbox yields a loud stderr note, never silent trust). Test: a forged row with the right fingerprint but wrong department/kind does NOT suppress the real escalation.
5. HIGH factory/launch.py ~:78 — the capability environment (systemd_user_probe → XDG_RUNTIME_DIR) is granted to ANY caller-supplied command, letting an arbitrary binary run mutating systemctl operations under the department's grant. Fix: when a department's charter declares ANY capability, launch.py must verify the launched command is python3 (sys.executable or a 'python3*' basename) executing a script whose realpath resolves INSIDE that department's runtime directory (departments/<dept>/runtime/) — otherwise refuse to launch with a clear error (capability-bearing environments only reach the department's own pinned runtime nodes). Departments with NO declared capabilities keep today's behavior. Update tests/test_launch_capabilities.py accordingly (in-runtime script gets the env; out-of-tree script or non-python command with a capability charter is refused; no-capability department unchanged).
6. MED test_watchdog_spine.py ~:243 + test_heal_lane.py — consume the remaining poisoned fixtures: feed fixtures/poisoned/unit_missing.json through the sense coverage self-check path (the inventory-gap poison must be caught), and fixtures/poisoned/non_allowlisted_playbook.json through heal_select (must refuse). Keep the forged_receipt waiver comment but strengthen it by pointing at the kernel receipt tests that DO consume signature forgeries (tests/ has kernel receipt coverage — cite the actual file name you find).

HOW TO RUN: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest departments/podcast/tests/ tests/ -q (everything must pass) && bash -n departments/podcast/runtime/podcast_daily.sh
